fields.description:
## Context

Project agents (reviewers, fix-bug, retro) currently operate against static defense artifacts (rubrics, planning gates, tests) in a non-static bug-class space. There is no artifact that asserts every known bug class is named in some defense layer, and no feedback loop turning escaped bugs into rubric/test/observability extensions. Discovery-channel data from `docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md` (repo-root-relative, read-only historical artifact) shows 16 of 22 recent closed bugs were caught at the release gate while code review caught only 3 of 37. Affected users: DSO maintainers and the agents themselves (orchestrator, /dso:fix-bug, /dso:retro, code-reviewer agents). Problem today: when a bug is caught downstream of review, no durable signal flows back to the rubric/test/observability layers. Outcome: shift bug detection earlier in the defense stack by making the bug-class map auditable, durable, and operationally connected. Replaces the original narrow scope of 4911-c7ba (six specific rubric items) with a categorical solution that subsumes those items as registry entries.

## Approach

Markdown registry seeded with a 27-slug, 9-group taxonomy (groups A-I: specification defects, environment portability, coupling and contract integrity, state and concurrency hazards, failure-mode and boundary defects, defense-system integrity, LLM/agent-orchestration defects, release and deploy hazards, operational state defects). Bash audit test asserts entry count, required fields, and defense_artifact_ref resolution. Haiku classifier sub-agent dispatched at /dso:fix-bug Phase G writes bug-type-<slug> tag with byte-exact schema validation and explicit failure-marker fallback. One-shot 60-day backfill script with single-run lock and tickets-branch assertion. /dso:retro adds aggregation step with MUST-surface labeled findings and positive-confirmation when no triggers fire.

## Success Criteria

1. Registry artifact at `plugins/dso/docs/bug-classification-registry.md` containing 27-slug 9-group taxonomy. Each entry has: slug (kebab-case), one-sentence classification question, primary defense layer (enum: planning_review, code_review, matrix_ci, coupling_test, concurrency_test, failure_path_test, defense_manifest_test, release_e2e, operational_process, prose_manifest_test), defense_artifact_ref with explicit prefix discriminator (`repo:`, `plugin:`, or `absolute:`), example tickets (>=2 where evidence exists), applies_to_project_classes enum (`all` or `agent_orchestration`).

2. Audit test parses the registry and asserts: (a) parsed entry count equals declared total (27 at seed time), (b) every entry has all required fields populated, (c) every `defense_artifact_ref` resolves (file present, named rubric section grep-matched, or test directory present). A mutation test confirms detection: a deliberately broken ref causes audit failure with a clear error identifying the broken slug.

3. `/dso:fix-bug` Phase G — Bug Classification (MANDATORY on `Fixed:` closure). The orchestrator MUST dispatch the bug-classifier-haiku agent on every closure with `--reason="Fixed:..."`. The sole exception is defined in the Skip block immediately below; no other skip exists. **Skip**: when the ticket was closed with `--reason="Escalated to user:..."` (keyed to reason prefix, NOT to whether code changed). Dispatch input: registry slug list with classification questions (unordered, one per line), bug title and description, fix diff summary. Output validation: orchestrator trims whitespace then byte-for-byte compares against `registry_slugs union {"uncategorized"}`; ANY deviation is schema failure (no fuzzy/normalization). Valid output writes `bug-type-<slug>` via the ticket tag CLI. Failure (schema/timeout/dispatch-error): MUST write BOTH `bug-type-uncategorized` AND `bug-type-classifier-failed-<reason>` where `<reason>` is one of `timeout`, `schema`, `dispatch-error` (dash-delimited, no colons). If a tag-write CLI call fails, retry once; on second failure, post a comment to the ticket recording the failure and treat the run as a protocol violation. Classifier prompt instructs: "Return a registry slug only if you would answer yes to its classification question with no caveats or conditionals; otherwise return `uncategorized`. Partial match is not a match."

4. Backfill script `backfill-bug-types.sh` iterates all bug tickets closed in the prior 60 days and applies the same classifier. Asserts tickets-branch presence at entry; uses a single-run lock under `.claude/locks/`; empty-list is a graceful no-op; idempotent re-run skips tickets already carrying any `bug-type-*` tag. Post-run, every closed bug in the 60-day window carries exactly one `bug-type-*` tag (the classifier-failed co-tag does not count toward the one-tag-per-bug rule). Backfill is implementation-splittable into a deferred-ok child task during preplanning if it complicates the registry + Phase G + retro delivery.

5. `/dso:retro` Bug Classification step (MANDATORY on every retro invocation). Calls `bug-classification-stats.sh --window-days <bug_classification.retro_window_days>` (default 60, aligned with the backfill window). Stats script uses `.claude/scripts/dso ticket list` (excludes deleted tickets) to aggregate `bug-type-*` tags. Config keys: `bug_classification.recurrence_threshold` (default 3), `bug_classification.retro_window_days` (default 60). Retro MUST surface EACH of these as a distinct, explicitly-labeled finding when its trigger fires; MUST NOT merge or inline into general retro prose:
   - (a) `bug-type-uncategorized` count >= threshold: "Uncategorized bug count: N. Consider proposing a new registry slug or revisiting existing slug definitions."
   - (b) any registry slug's count >= threshold: "Slug recurrence: <slug> has N occurrences in the window. Revisit mitigation strategy."
   - (c) ANY `bug-type-classifier-failed-*` tag present in the window (fires when count >= 1; threshold fixed at 1, NOT configurable): "Classifier failures detected: N tickets carry bug-type-classifier-failed-*. Run diagnostic."

   When no trigger fires, MUST emit explicit positive confirmation: "Bug classification health: no threshold breaches in this window." Silence is not acceptable. Within-session validation: post-backfill retro run on real backfilled data fires >=1 surfacing prompt OR emits the "no threshold breaches" confirmation; operator confirms before sprint closure.

## Out of Scope

- Code-reviewer agent rubric alignment with registry slug values (filed as follow-on a47f-b451-8f4c-46b1).
- Replay-corpus mechanical validation (a72d-df57-ac6e-4073, follow-on, depends_on this epic).
- Closed-loop automated rubric expansion (level c, not yet scheduled).

## Delivery checklist (not SCs)

- Registry + audit test ship in the same PR (no commit-order window).
- New `.sh` files chmod'd at creation.

## Coordination notes (relates_to)

- a72d-df57 — Level-b replay corpus follow-on; depends_on this epic.
- a47f-b451 — Code-reviewer rubric alignment follow-on; scrutiny:pending stub.
- 1de7-50d4 — Resolution-enum epic; both add fields at /dso:fix-bug Phase G. Coordinate ordering: resolution writes a closure field, this epic writes a tag; both are additive.
- 99f1-153c — fix-bug recurrence prevention; bug-type-* tags feed antipattern detection.
- 371f-cfc3 — DSO ticket system packaging; audit test depends on stable ticket CLI contract.
- 5df7-63ac, 853a-c719 — observability epics; stats-script patterns may converge.
- 7575-5a90 — static-analysis defense layer; audit test registers with framework if/when it lands.
- cfb3-3f53 — ticket compaction; retro step ordering (classification before snapshot).
- w21-bsnz — legacy-code remediation; taxonomy alignment opportunity.

## Reframe note

This epic was originally scoped as "Reviewer rubric expansion: platform, runner, hermeticity, config, pipefail dimensions" — adding six specific named rubric items. During the 2026-05-11 brainstorm session, scope was broadened to a categorical solution (this spec). The original six items become registry entries under groups B (environment-portability, strict-mode-survival), C (paired-artifact-coupling), and F (defense-integrity), where the audit test asserts each has a primary defense layer with a resolved defense_artifact_ref.

## Provenance

See docs/observed-failure-patterns-4-26.md, docs/process-gaps-4-26.md, docs/proposed-mitigations-4-26.md, docs/new-epics-4-26.md for the original failure-pattern analysis and gap discovery. The categorical reframe and 27-slug taxonomy emerged during the 2026-05-11 brainstorm session (broadened from the original 6 mitigations into 9 groups covering polyglot bug classes).
